lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, point and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for focused listening, accurate pointing to the specific fruits or vegetables, and clear, confident repetition.
“Let’s go to the market today! I need to  buy some food to cook for dinner.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - C. Look and say

details: Look and say provides controlled practice using the target structure to describe possession. Students apply the grammar rules for ‘some’ and ‘any’ to describe the presence of items in the market stalls.
Look for accurate use of ‘got some’ and ‘hasn't got any’, correct food vocabulary, and clear pronunciation of the target sentences.
“I want to buy mushrooms to make soup, but I can’t find them. Can you look and tell me who has got some?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - D. Stick. Then ask and answer. 10m]

details: Stick. Then ask and answer combines listening comprehension with speaking practice. Students place stickers to show understanding, then use the visuals to ask and answer questions about possession.
Look for correct sticker placement, accurate use of ‘What has he/she got?’, and clear pronunciation.
“Here are our friends. It looks like they have finished shopping! Let’s find out what they  have bought.”

The chant consolidates target vocabulary and grammar through rhythm and repetition. It allows students to practise natural intonation and sentence stress in a fun, high-energy closer.
Look for enthusiastic participation, clear pronunciation of the target questions, and correct rhythm and intonation from the whole class.
“That was a great trip to the market! I’m excited to cook dinner tonight!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.

Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
